findings.evidence: Roadmap lines 439–444 require that specialized `peterWeylBasis` “is `fourierBasis` (up to the indexing equivalence)”; the only concluding declaration, lines 194–207, has an AE function-equality conclusion and never mentions `fourierBasis`.
findings.fix: Add a theorem equating the reindexed Hilbert bases after transporting along `haarProb_eq_haarAddCircle` (and the multiplicative/additive type identification), using this AE lemma to prove equality of basis vectors.
findings.issue: `coeFn_peterWeylBasis_fourier` only identifies AE representatives pointwise; it does not expose an equality between the reindexed `peterWeylBasis` and Mathlib's `AddCircle.fourierBasis`, which is the roadmap's stated public product.

findings.evidence: The file provides `fourierIrrepModel_dim`, `fourierIrrepModel_rep_apply`, `fourierPeterWeylIndexEquiv_apply`, and a symmetric-index lemma at lines 83–145; no downstream computational use requiring either exposed body is established.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` annotations; add any missing accessor theorem needed to prove the actual basis equality instead of making consumers unfold these constructions.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` publishes the bodies of both `fourierIrrepModel` (line 74) and `fourierPeterWeylIndexEquiv` (line 119), although their characteristic behavior is already intended to be provided through named lemmas.

summary: The public API stops at representatives of individual vectors and exposes two implementation bodies unnecessarily, so it does not provide the promised canonical basis identification.
